extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling reexamination, reissue, interference, or related proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and Office policies governing concurrent ex parte reexamination, inter partes reexamination, interferences, reissue applications, and related petitions, notices, suspensions, mergers, and fees before the USPTO/Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding before the Office, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved such as interferences, reissues, ex parte reexaminations, inter partes reexaminations, or litigation and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.985 for notification of prior or concurrent proceedings in an inter partes reexamination proceeding. This requirement is to keep the Office informed of activity relevant to reexamination and to reduce procedural surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to suspend reexamination or interference (37 CFR 1.565(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in the process of ex parte reexamination is or becomes involved in an interference, the Director may suspend the reexamination or the interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will not consider a request to suspend an interference unless a motion (§ 41.121(a)(3)) to suspend the interference has been presented to, and denied by, an administrative patent judge, and the request is filed within ten (10) days of a decision by an administrative patent judge denying the motion for suspension or such other time as the administrative patent judge may set. For concurrent inter partes reexamination and interference of a patent, see § 1.993.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices in Board proceedings (37 CFR 41.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at the initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify: (1) its real party-in-interest, and (2) each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect, or be affected by, the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal and include a copy. See also §§ 1.301 to 1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of examination before contested case (37 CFR 41.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated, except as the Board may otherwise authorize, for each involved application and patent: (a) examination or reexamination must be completed, and (b) there must be at least one claim that: (1) is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case, and (2) would be involved in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures there is an examinable claim that remains if the contested issue resolves against the party; used to determine readiness for Board contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction over involved files (37 CFR 41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board acquires jurisdiction over any involved file when the Board initiates a contested case. Other proceedings for the involved file within the Office are suspended except as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once Board jurisdiction attaches, Office actions in other proceedings are generally stayed unless the Board directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: reexamination will not be delayed for interference (35 U.S.C. 305 special dispatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy of the Office is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed, or stayed, because of an interference or the possibility of an interference due to the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305 that all reexamination proceedings be conducted with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will make required decisions in the reexamination while also proceeding with the interference to the extent desirable; 37 CFR 41.103 gives the Board flexibility to tailor solutions for copending matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceeding is not a party to an interference (35 U.S.C. 135(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a patent being reexamined may become involved in an interference proceeding with at least one application, the reexamination proceeding itself can never be involved in an interference proceeding; an interference may be declared only with respect to an application or an unexpired patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites statutory language: interference declared when 'an application is made for a patent which... would interfere with any pending application, or with any unexpired patent' — reexamination is neither an application nor a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provoking an interference via amendment in an application (apply 37 CFR 41.202(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a pending application seeking to provoke an interference with a patent under reexamination, the involved applicant must comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a), including identifying the patent under reexamination with which interference is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding application claims may be rejected on any applicable ground including prior art cited in reexamination. Prosecution should continue; if application is placed in condition for allowance and still contains claims which interfere, an interference should ordinarily be proposed. Examiner must notify OPLA before proposing and may not propose unless authorized by OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of an application when interference not authorized; use of form paragraph 23.16
rubrics_metrics.description: If the interference is not authorized (e.g., resolution of an issue in the reexamination proceeding is necessary to the interference), further action on the application should be suspended until the certificate on the reexamination proceeding has been issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 23.16 may be used to notify applicant of the suspension. After certificate issuance, examiner should review and then evaluate whether to propose interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review after reexamination certificate issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the reexamination certificate has issued and been published, the examiner should review the certificate to see if it makes any changes in the patent claims and then evaluate whether the patent still contains claims which interfere with claims of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims still interfere, the examiner should propose an interference. See MPEP Chapter 2300 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to suspend interference pending reexamination (37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) / 41.123(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination may be made at any time during the interference by any party thereto. The motion must be presented to the administrative patent judge who will decide the motion based on the particular fact situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is not favored; normally no consideration will be given until a reexamination order is issued, nor will suspension normally be permitted until after motions in the interference have been disposed of. If denied by the APJ, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.565(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of interference decided by Chief APJ
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to stay an interference under 37 CFR 1.565(e) will be decided by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific chain of authority for requests to stay an interference pending reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a request for reexamination during an interference (37 CFR 1.510(a); 41.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, file a request for reexamination. Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), the patent owner must notify the Board that a request for reexamination was filed, within 20 days of receiving notice of the request having been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will be processed normally; no delay or stay of the reexamination will occur because the requester is not a party to the interference. If an examiner orders reexamination and subsequently rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the Board's attention shall be called thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of interference when interference declared while reexamination ongoing (file notice per 1.565 and 41.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.565, the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding before the Office is required to notify the Office when the patent being reexamined becomes involved in an interference; the patent owner must file in the reexamination proceeding a paper giving notice of the interference proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are designed to keep the Office and appropriate parties informed and to eliminate procedural surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to stay reexamination because of interference — timing and standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered, but will be returned to the party submitting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to stay may be filed by the patent owner as part of the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or subsequent thereto. If a party to the interference other than the patent owner is the requester, that party may petition to stay as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535. A party other than the requester has no standing (37 CFR 1.550(g)); premature petitions are returned by CRU or TC Director. Decisions on merits of petitions to stay reexamination because of an interference will be made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board notification of changes to claims after reexamination certificate (action in interference following reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by the issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified. Upon issuance and publication of the reexamination certificate, the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification is required so interference proceedings can take account of claim changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger or stay when reissue application and ex parte reexamination are concurrent (37 CFR 1.565(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination proceeding on which an order pursuant to § 1.525 has been mailed are pending concurrently on a patent, a decision will usually be made to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one of the two proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where merger ordered, merged examination conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171–1.179 and the patent owner will be required to place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the ex parte reexamination proceeding during the pendency of the merged proceeding. An ex parte reexamination merged with a reissue application shall be concluded by the grant of the reissued patent. OPLA decides merger or stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner notification responsibilities for concurrent reissue and reexamination (37 CFR 1.178(b), 1.565(a), 1.985)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding are pending concurrently on a patent, the patent owner has a responsibility to notify the Office of such by filing a Notification of Concurrent Proceedings as early as possible in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File in the reissue application a Notification pursuant to 37 CFR 1.178(b) and in the reexamination proceeding a Notification pursuant to 37 CFR 1.565(a) or 1.985 as appropriate. If paper files exist, they should be hand-delivered to OPLA when notifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for decision on merging or staying proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether or not to merge the reissue application examination and reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of the two proceedings, will not be made prior to the mailing of an order to reexamine the patent pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525, and the expiration of the statement-reply period following the order to reexamine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until such time, reissue examination proceeds. Determinations must not be delayed because of a copending reissue application due to statutory timing (35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515 requiring determinations within 3 months after filing a request). CRU SPRS or TC QAS will notify OPLA when ready for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for merging vs staying — case-by-case analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on whether to merge the proceedings or stay a proceeding will be made on a case-by-case basis based upon the various proceedings. The status of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding will be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) reissue about to issue — delay determination until reissue granted and base reexamination on reissue claims; (B) reissue pending — merge narrower reexamination with broader reissue when desirable; (C) reexamination underway — consider status such as appeals or Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate. Cases on appeal or to courts alter merger likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when reissue issues before reexamination determination (use reissue claims as starting point; form paragraph 22.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent issues before determination on the reexamination request must be made, the determination should normally be delayed until after the granting of the reissue patent; the reexamination, if ordered, would then be on the reissue patent claims rather than the original patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination starting claims must be presented as a 'clean copy' (bracketed words absent, added words not italicized). Where reissue patent has issued, use form paragraph 22.05 to state subsequent proceedings will be based on reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain identical amendments in merged reissue/reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments in the reissue application and the reexamination file for purposes of the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present when merger ordered, patent owner must submit a 'housekeeping' amendment placing same amendments in both proceedings. Housekeeping amendments must not address any issue of patentability. Amendments are submitted under 37 CFR 1.173 in accordance with reissue practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner conduct and form of Office actions in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application examination and a reexamination proceeding are merged, each Office action issued by the examiner will take the form of a single action which jointly applies to both the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, and each action will be physically entered into both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should prepare an Office action at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding. Responses by applicant/patent owner must consist of a single response filed in duplicate for entry in both files (or multiple copies if multiple reexaminations merged). Service copies must be made on any third party reexamination requester; copies of Office actions mailed to the third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely and appropriately respond in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner in a merged proceeding fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, then the merger will be automatically dissolved (severed). The reissue application will be held abandoned. A NIRC will be issued, and the Director will proceed to issue a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office, unless further action is clearly needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express abandonment of the reissue application will dissolve the merger and continue the reexamination proceeding. Filing a CPA that effects express abandonment likely dissolves the merger and stays the CPA/reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of dissolution based on abandonment — adjust grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the merged proceeding is dissolved based on abandonment of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding continues, any grounds of rejection which are not applicable under reexamination should be withdrawn and any new grounds of rejection which are applicable under reexamination should be made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of questions not proper for reexamination should be noted by the examiner as not being proper under 37 CFR 1.552(c). There is no guarantee a continuation reissue will be merged later; policy prevents delay tactics by patent owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an RCE in reissue application on merger
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant/patent owner files a request for continued examination (RCE) of the reissue application under 37 CFR 1.114, then the merger will be automatically dissolved (severed), and the reissue application will then be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners are put on notice that RCE practice is not available in reexamination; responses in the reexamination must be made taking into account the non-availability of RCE. Failure to timely respond results in termination under 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge or stay — when to file and who may file (37 CFR 1.182)
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or stay one of them because of the other, should be filed before an order granting reexamination is issued because the Office will generally, sua sponte, make a decision to merge or stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or stay at time of patent owner’s statement under 1.530 or subsequent thereto if Office has not acted. A third party requester does not have standing to file a petition to merge (cannot be a party to reissue); third party may file a notification of concurrent proceedings or may petition to stay the reexamination it requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time fee, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be filed for entry in each file in the merged proceeding. As to excess claim fees, reissue practice will control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of reexamination because of litigation (37 CFR 1.565(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in the process of ex parte reexamination is or becomes involved in litigation, the Director shall determine whether or not to suspend the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 302 permits an ex parte reexamination request to be filed at any time; the Manual provides guidelines governing Office handling of ex parte reexamination requests where there is concurrent litigation, including court-ordered or sanctioned reexamination, litigation stayed for reexamination, or extended pendency concurrent with litigation.
